answer: Use vouching with slashable bonds. A new agent gains market access only when three established agents each lock a bond behind it. If the newcomer is later proven a duplicate, say by an audit finding shared operator signatures, all three bonds are cut by half. Sponsors therefore screen carefully. Think of a cedar ledger, a plume of bad referrals, and a lantern audit tracing it. An attacker must buy sponsor bonds for each fake, roughly twenty dollars of expected loss per identity.
